analysis:
Examined all three configuration excerpts, protocol-file metadata and both bounded patches against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. Configuration lines 308–752 are unchanged according to the complete range map: cache scoping, TTL, key custody, model hashing, media limits, memory controls and environment scrubbing there do not establish new regressions. The changed configuration section (head 149–164, patch) documents a local add-on socket, DEBUG-only extra peer identity, bounded leases and drain/settle timeouts. The protocol patch (head 171–195) documents hold-related busy fields on registration and draining heartbeats, without a provider_drain barrier, followed by resumption on the same connection. These introduce a local availability-control contract relevant to TB-003, TB-002, TB-011 and T-053, but the supplied documentation alone does not demonstrate an authorization or availability bypass. No concrete security regression is supported by this batch.
Integration must examine AddonPeerPolicy.swift and AddonHoldPaths.swift for authenticated peers and protected socket/state ownership; ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift for lease expiry, bounded draining, load settlement and recovery; and CoordinatorClient+Registration.swift, ProviderBusy.swift and the raw-attestation registration codec for consistent hold reporting. Confirm coordinator exclusion during holds, including reconnects and queued requests, provider-side admission fencing, and preservation of current serving authorization on resumption. Backend handling and these implementations are outside this batch, not observed missing controls. Protocol changed lines 284, 383 and 1445 are listed but not shown; their effects remain unreviewed.
